findings.body:
## Zarr v3 storage basis and breadth of allowed Zarr features

**Finding.** OME-Zarr 0.5 is implemented on version 3 of the Zarr specification, and all Zarr features (codecs, chunk grids, chunk key encodings, data types, storage transformers) may be used in a conforming fileset unless explicitly disallowed by the OME-Zarr specification (S003 lines 67-72). Chunk files conform to the Zarr array specification and the metadata in each array's `zarr.json` (lines 99-100). The hierarchy may be stored locally, on a web server accessed via HTTP, or in object storage such as S3 or GCS (lines 73-77).

**Governing conditions.** Normative for what a conforming fileset may contain: a reader that supports only a subset of Zarr v3 codecs, chunk grids, or data types will encounter conforming files it cannot decode.

**Sources.** S003, OME-Zarr 0.5 Final Community Group Report (8 September 2026), frozen capture sha256 5d8b240877ed2cf9596566187bcb3779ea011d5319807134c65e2e7dc2ae82de (896 lines, 36980 bytes), alias URI https://ngff.openmicroscopy.org/0.5/ ; locators: lines 67-77, 99-100.

**Implications.** Slide Scout needs an embedded Zarr v3 reader; codec-support breadth is a compatibility risk and a product decision to scope explicitly. Responsiveness with large datasets rests on chunk-aligned partial reads, which the chunk-file model supports. HTTP/S3 storage statements transfer only conceptually because the product boundary is local filesystem reading.

**Uncertainty.** The Zarr v3 specification itself is only referenced, not included in the capture, so chunk/codec/storage-transformer semantics are asserted by reference. Which codecs real writer tools actually emit is unknown from this capture; no live implementation research was permitted in this assignment.

## Image hierarchy: group layout, arbitrary level names, dimension ordering

**Finding.** Each OME-Zarr image is a Zarr group whose group-level attributes live in `zarr.json` and include `multiscales` and (optionally) `omero` (S003 lines 87-89). Each multiscale resolution level is a separate Zarr array; array names are arbitrary with ordering defined by the `multiscales` metadata, though often a sequence starting at 0 (lines 91-94). Image arrays must be up to 5-dimensional with the axis of type time before type channel before spatial axes (lines 96-97). Dimension count is variable between 2 and 5 and axis names are arbitrary (line 81). An optional `labels` group sits at the same level as the resolution arrays and holds a list of label images; label dimensions must equal the corresponding image dimension or be 1 if irrelevant (lines 102-108); intermediate folders are permitted and contain no extra metadata (line 110); label multiscale arrays support only integer values (lines 116-117).

**Governing conditions.** Level ordering comes from metadata, not names: a reader sorting directories like `0,1,2` lexically or numerically without consulting `multiscales.datasets` can present pyramids in the wrong order. Time-before-channel-before-space array axis order is an obligation on data, which the viewer can rely on only after confirming the axes metadata (F05, F08).

**Sources.** S003 capture (see F01 for version pin), locators: lines 78-117 (section 1.1 Images), especially 81, 87-94, 96-97, 102-108, 110, 116-117.

**Implications.** The plan's fileset opening and listing must be metadata-driven: discover images by finding groups with `multiscales`, resolve pyramid levels via `datasets[].path` order, and never infer semantics from folder names. The `labels` container layout is the discovery route for overlays (see F10).

**Uncertainty.** The capture's layout description is illustrative prose around the normative metadata sections; behavior for unexpected extra groups or arrays next to an image is only addressed for bioformats2raw collections (F06: readers MAY ignore other groups).

## High-content screening (HCS) hierarchy: plate, row, well, field of view

**Finding.** For HCS datasets, three groups MUST be defined above the images: the group above the images is a well and MUST implement the `well` specification; the group above the well is a row; the group above the row is a plate that MUST implement the `plate` specification (S003 lines 119-127). A well row group SHOULD NOT be present if there are no images in that row, and a well group SHOULD NOT be present if there are no images in the well (lines 128-129). All images in a well are fields of view of the same well (lines 121-123). The example hierarchy shows plate zarr.json, row directories, column directories implementing `well`, and per-field groups implementing `multiscales` and `omero` with their own resolution levels and optional `labels` (lines 132-148).

**Governing conditions.** MUST-level: well and plate groups implement their specifications (detail in F11, F12). SHOULD-level: empty rows/wells SHOULD NOT exist, so a conforming fileset may legitimately be sparse; the viewer cannot assume a full rectangular grid.

**Sources.** S003 capture (version pin in F01), locators: lines 118-148 (section 1.2 High-content screening).

**Implications.** Image discovery inside a fileset must traverse plate, then rows, then wells, then fields of view, and enumerate fields via `well.images`, not by scanning directories. Sparse plates (only some wells present) are expected, not exceptional. Field groups are ordinary multiscale images, so once selected they reuse the normal image pipeline.

**Uncertainty.** The capture does not state whether extra intermediate groups under a well are permitted; directory scanning beyond `well.images` risks false discovery, but the normative listing rule lives in F12.

## OME metadata namespace and version consistency

**Finding.** OME-Zarr metadata is stored in the various `zarr.json` files throughout the hierarchy, under the namespaced key `ome` inside `attributes`; the metadata version is a string in the `version` attribute within the `ome` namespace (S003 lines 152-165). The OME-Zarr Metadata version MUST be consistent within a hierarchy (line 156).

**Governing conditions.** MUST: version consistency within one hierarchy. A fileset mixing, say, `0.4` and `0.5` `ome.version` values is non-conforming, and detecting it is a legitimate validation the viewer can surface rather than silently guessing semantics.

**Sources.** S003 capture (version pin in F01), locators: lines 149-165 (section 2 opening), especially 152-156, 157-165 (example).

**Implications.** The viewer should read `attributes.ome.version` on every node it opens, treat inconsistency as malformed input with an explanatory message (matching the plan's Slice 03/05 failure-feedback requirement), and use the version to gate 0.5-specific behavior such as the `dimension_names` obligation (F05).

**Uncertainty.** The capture does not define reader behavior when versions are inconsistent (reject vs best-effort) - that is a product decision; and real-world mixed-version filesets may exist even though they are non-conforming (no capture evidence either way).

## Axes metadata: names, types, units, dimension_names

**Finding.** `axes` is a list of dictionaries describing the dimensions of a physical coordinate space. Each dictionary MUST contain `name`, with values unique across all `name` fields; SHOULD contain `type`, one of `space`, `time`, `channel`, but MAY take other custom string values; SHOULD contain `unit`, whose value SHOULD be a UDUNITS-2 valid string (S003 lines 167-170). Explicit allowed unit vocabularies are enumerated for space axes (angstrom through zettameter, lines 171) and time axes (attosecond through zettasecond, line 172). The length of `axes` MUST equal the number of dimensions of the arrays holding the image data (line 173). The `dimension_names` attribute MUST be included in the `zarr.json` of the Zarr array of each multiscale level and MUST match the names in the `axes` metadata (line 174).

**Governing conditions.** MUST: unique names; axes length equals array dimensionality; `dimension_names` present in array metadata and matching `axes`. SHOULD (not guaranteed): `type` and `unit` present and standard - a conforming file can omit units or use custom axis types.

**Sources.** S003 capture (version pin in F01), locators: lines 166-174 (section 2.1 axes metadata).

**Implications.** The details panel can show calibrated coordinates only when units exist; absence of units (SHOULD-level) requires a defined fallback such as displaying raw index coordinates labeled as uncalibrated - a product decision the thin plan does not make. Channel/time/plane controls should classify axes by `type` with a graceful path for custom types (e.g., treat unknown types as non-spatial). `dimension_names` gives the viewer a cheap integrity check on level arrays.

**Uncertainty.** UDUNITS-2 parsing/conversion rules are not in the capture; display formatting and any unit conversion (e.g., micrometer to millimeter) is unspecified. Behavior when `type` is absent or custom is a product choice.

## bioformats2raw.layout transitional collections and reader obligations for multi-image filesets

**Finding.** Transitional `bioformats2raw.layout` metadata identifies a group that implicitly describes a series of images, added in v0.4 to specify filesets that already exist in the wild; an upcoming NGFF specification will replace it (S003 lines 175-181). Layout: top-level `zarr.json` with the layout key, an `OME` group holding `series` metadata and `METADATA.ome.xml`, and consecutively numbered image groups `0`, `1`, ... (lines 182-191). Conforming groups MUST have value `3` for the `bioformats2raw.layout` key at the top of the hierarchy (line 256) and SHOULD have OME-XML in `OME/METADATA.ome.xml` adhering to the OME-XML specification with `<MetadataOnly/>` rather than `<BinData/>`, `<BinaryOnly/>` or `<TiffData/>` (lines 257-260). If the top-level group is a plate, the `plate` key MUST also be present, takes precedence, and parsing should follow the plate specification; mixing image collections with plates is not possible (lines 204-206). Image-location logic: with `plate` metadata, images MUST be at the defined locations; `series` SHOULD be provided for tools unaware of plates; if the `OME` group has `series`, it MUST be a list of strings, each a path to an image group, whose order MUST match the order of `Image` elements in the OME-XML if provided; if no `series` and no plate, separate `multiscales` images MUST be stored in consecutively numbered groups starting from 0, each representing exactly one OME-XML Image in the same order (lines 261-270). Reader obligations: readers SHOULD make users aware of more than one image (SHOULD NOT default to only opening the first); MAY use `series`; MAY show all images or offer a choice, as with HCS plates; MAY ignore other groups or arrays under the root (lines 271-275).

**Governing conditions.** MUST: layout value `3`; series as string list; order constraints; numbered-groups fallback. SHOULD: surface multiple images to the user rather than silently opening the first; OME-XML details. MAY: choice of presentation and ignoring unrelated groups.

**Sources.** S003 capture (version pin in F01), locators: lines 175-275 (section 2.2, including 2.2.1 Layout, 2.2.2 Attributes, 2.2.3 Details), especially 204-206, 256-275.

**Implications.** This is the strongest normative support for the brief requirement to find images within a fileset and the plan sentence that the app lists the images it finds: a listing UI is not just nice-to-have, readers SHOULD NOT default to the first image. Real tool output (bioformats2raw) uses this layout, so Slice 04 interop requires it. Plate-precedence means collection detection must check `plate` before treating the fileset as a series collection.

**Uncertainty.** OME-XML content rules reference the OME-XML specification, which is outside the capture; the future replacement metadata for this transitional layout is unspecified here, so long-term compatibility is open.

## coordinateTransformations vocabulary and application order

**Finding.** `coordinateTransformations` describe transformations mapping between coordinate spaces defined by `axes`, for example mapping a discrete data space of an array to the corresponding physical space (S003 lines 277-278). It is a list of dictionaries; each entry MUST contain `type`, whose value MUST be one of: `identity` (the default, typically not explicitly defined), `translation`, or `scale` (lines 279-283). `translation` and `scale` each store a vector either inline as `translation`/`scale` lists of floats or as binary data at a location in this container via `path` (lines 284-289); the vector length defines the number of dimensions (lines 286, 289). Transformations in the list are applied sequentially and in order (line 293).

**Governing conditions.** MUST: each entry has a valid `type`. The inline-versus-`path` alternative is part of the normative field table, so conforming files may store transforms as binary data by path. Sequential application order is normative.

**Sources.** S003 capture (version pin in F01), locators: lines 276-293 (section 2.3 coordinateTransformations metadata).

**Implications.** Correct calibrated coordinates require composing dataset-level then group-level transforms (order fixed in F08) as sequential operations: physical = scale applied to index, plus translation, in list order. Supporting only inline arrays and silently misreading `path`-based transforms would produce wrong coordinates for conforming files; supporting `path`-form is therefore a correctness requirement for full conformance, though its practical frequency is unknown (product scoping decision with a documented limitation if deferred).

**Uncertainty.** The capture does not specify the binary layout (array name, dtype, byte order) of `path`-referenced transform data; implementing it needs assumptions or future source work. This is an unresolved area.

## multiscales metadata: pyramid obligations and calibration rules

**Finding.** Image metadata lives under the `multiscales` key in group-level OME-Zarr metadata; an image is 2 to 5 dimensional data with optional time or channel axes, stored in multiple resolutions (S003 lines 295-298). Each `multiscales` dictionary MUST contain `axes` (line 299) whose length must be 2-5 and equal the dimensionality of the arrays (line 300); axes MUST contain 2 or 3 `space` entries and MAY add one `time` and one `channel` or null/custom-type entry (line 301); entries MUST be ordered time first, then channel/custom, then space, matching array dimension order (line 302); for three spatial axes stacked along z, order SHOULD be `zyx` (line 303). Each dictionary MUST contain `datasets`, a list describing resolution levels (line 304); each dataset MUST contain `path` relative to the current group, ordered from largest (highest resolution) to smallest (lines 305-306); all datasets MUST have the same number of dimensions, not more than 5, matching `axes` (line 307). Each dataset MUST contain `coordinateTransformations` mapping data coordinates to physical coordinates for that level; transformations MUST only be of type translation or scale; they MUST contain exactly one scale transformation specifying pixel size in physical units or time duration, or, when scaling is unavailable for an axis, the factor versus the first resolution defaulting to 1.0 (lines 308-310); MAY contain exactly one translation, which MUST be listed after scale (lines 311-312); scale and translation array lengths MUST equal the axes length (line 312). Each `multiscales` dictionary MAY contain group-level `coordinateTransformations` applied to all levels after the dataset-level ones, under the same type/order rules (lines 314-316). SHOULD fields: `name` (line 317), `type` of downscaling method (line 318), `metadata` about the method (line 319); a full example with per-level scales and a group-level time scale appears at lines 320-387. When multiple multiscales entries exist, the user can choose by name with the first as fallback; pseudocode at lines 388-397.

**Governing conditions.** MUST: axes; datasets; path order largest-to-smallest; exactly one scale per dataset; translation (if any) after scale; length equalities; dimension constraints. SHOULD: `zyx` spatial order; name/type/metadata fields. MAY: group-level transforms; translation at all.

**Sources.** S003 capture (version pin in F01), locators: lines 294-397 (section 2.4 multiscales metadata).

**Implications.** The plan's pyramid-level selection must enumerate `datasets` in listed order (largest first) and pick by view fit/chunk cost; level ordering and count are normative. Physical calibration is always derivable in principle because scale is mandatory (defaulting to 1.0), so the details panel can always compute data-to-physical mapping, composing dataset-level then group-level transforms in order. Multiple named multiscales require a chooser or a documented first-entry fallback. Channel/time/plane detection follows the axes type ordering rule.

**Uncertainty.** Behavior for non-conforming cases (zero or multiple scale transforms, wrong vector lengths) is undefined in the capture - detection is product work; whether real writers emit group-level transforms or translations is unmeasured here.

## omero metadata (transitional): channel rendering hints

**Finding.** Transitional rendering information for channels is found under the `omero` key in group-level metadata (S003 lines 398-400). Example structure (lines 401-425) shows `channels` array matching the c dimension size, each channel with `color` (6 hex digits RGB), `label`, `active`, `window` with `min`/`max`/`start`/`end`, plus `rdefs` with `defaultT`, `defaultZ`, and `model` (`color` or `greyscale`), and a pointer to the OMERO WebGateway documentation. Normative text: `omero` is optional, but if present it MUST contain `channels`, an array of dictionaries describing the channels; each channel dictionary MUST contain `color` (a string of 6 hexadecimal digits) and MUST contain `window`, which MUST contain `min` and `max` and also `start` and `end` (lines 426-430).

**Governing conditions.** MUST (conditional on presence): `channels`; per-channel `color` and `window` with `min`/`max`/`start`/`end`. Optional overall: the whole `omero` key. The `rdefs` defaults appear only inside the informative example, and the semantics are delegated to the OMERO WebGateway documentation (lines 424-425) - treat defaultT/defaultZ/model as de-facto conventions, not MUST-level obligations of this specification.

**Sources.** S003 capture (version pin in F01), locators: lines 398-430 (section 2.5 omero metadata, transitional).

**Implications.** Channel visibility controls, channel colors, and sensible initial time/plane selection can be driven by `omero` when present - directly serving the plan's channel controls and the brief's channel inspection requirement - but because the key is optional and transitional, the viewer needs defined fallbacks (e.g., greyscale or a default color cycle, first time point and central plane) as a product decision. Transitional status means future NGFF versions may drop it (reading support is what transitional policy expects, F13); the viewer should not build novel semantics on it beyond display hints.

**Uncertainty.** Exact interpretation of window min/max versus start/end and of `model` is defined in external OMERO documentation not included in the capture; channel-count mismatch with the actual c axis is a malformed case with no defined handling here.

## labels and image-label: overlay discovery, dtypes, colors, alignment

**Finding.** Label images are pixel-annotation arrays with integer values of custom meaning, stored in a `labels` group nested within the image group at the same level as the resolution arrays (S003 lines 431-437). Label pixels MUST be one of the integer dtypes [uint8, int8, uint16, int16, uint32, int32, uint64, int64] (lines 438-439). Intermediate groups between `labels` and the images are allowed but MUST NOT contain metadata; label image names are arbitrary (lines 439-440). The `labels` group `zarr.json` MUST contain a `labels` key whose value is a JSON array of paths to the labeled multiscale image(s); all label images SHOULD be listed (lines 441-443); the hierarchy overview also states labels will be listed with the example { labels: [ original/0 ] } (lines 104-105). The label image `zarr.json` MUST implement the multiscales specification, and its `datasets` MUST have the same number of entries (scale levels) as the original unlabeled image (lines 454-455). The label image metadata SHOULD contain `image-label`, whose `colors` key MUST be a JSON array of color objects and whose `version` MUST be a string; conforming readers SHOULD display labels using the specified colors; each colors object MUST contain integer `label-value` and MAY contain `rgba` (four integers 0-255, the fourth being alpha); additional keys are allowed (lines 456-466). The `image-label` object MAY contain `properties` (array of objects each MUST contain integer `label-value`, plus arbitrary key-value metadata; keys need not be consistent across objects) and `source` (object; `image` key MUST be a string relative path to the source Zarr image group, default `../../`) (lines 467-474); example at lines 475-514 with rendered color/opacity explanation at lines 513-514. Label dimensions must equal the corresponding image dimension or be 1 (lines 106-108).

**Governing conditions.** MUST: integer dtypes; `labels` key listing paths; label image implements multiscales with the same level count as the original; `label-value` integers; `rgba` values 0-255 when present; `source.image` a string path when present. SHOULD: all labels listed; `image-label` present; readers display with specified colors.

**Sources.** S003 capture (version pin in F01), locators: lines 431-514 (section 2.6 labels metadata) plus 102-117 (layout), 104-105 (listing example).

**Implications.** Overlay support in the plan maps directly onto this machinery: discover overlays via the `labels` list, align level-for-level (equal level counts are guaranteed), and color by `colors[].rgba` with alpha compositing (the example uses alpha 128, i.e., 50 percent). Because listing all labels is only SHOULD, a viewer that trusts the list alone can miss labels - a false-dismissal risk; scanning the `labels` tree as a supplement is a product decision. Non-integer label arrays are non-conforming and can be rejected with a clear message.

**Uncertainty.** Rendering semantics when `image-label` or `colors` are absent are unspecified (product fallback needed); whether rgba needs premultiplication or a specific blend mode is not stated; interaction between label dims of size 1 and per-plane overlay display is left to the implementer.

## plate metadata: field obligations for HCS navigation

**Finding.** The plate dictionary lives under the `plate` key in the plate group's metadata (S003 lines 515-517). Obligations: `acquisitions` MAY be present; its objects MUST contain `id` (unique integer >= 0 within the plate) and SHOULD contain `name` (MUST be string) and `maximumfieldcount` (MUST be positive integer), MAY contain `description`, and MAY contain `starttime`/`endtime` (MUST be integer epoch timestamps) (lines 518-529). `columns` MUST be present as a list; every physical column MUST be defined even if no wells exist in it; each column MUST contain `name` (string, alphanumeric only, case-sensitive, unique in the list), with care SHOULD be taken to avoid collisions on case-insensitive filesystems (lines 530-537). `field_count` SHOULD be present (value MUST be a positive integer, the maximum fields per view across all wells) (lines 538-539). `name` SHOULD be present (string) (lines 540-541). `rows` MUST be present with the same naming rules as columns (lines 542-549). `version` MUST be present, a string for the plate specification version (lines 550-551). `wells` MUST be present; each well MUST contain `path` (string: row name + / + column name, in that order, no extra leading or trailing directories) and both `rowIndex` and `columnIndex` (0-based integers into the rows/columns lists); path, rowIndex and columnIndex MUST all refer to the same row/column pair (lines 552-560). Worked examples: dense 2x3 plate with two acquisitions (lines 561-640) and a sparse plate with 2 wells in a 12x8 grid (lines 641-739).

**Governing conditions.** MUST: `columns`, `rows`, `version`, `wells` with their field constraints; acquisition id uniqueness; 0-based indices; path shape. SHOULD: `field_count`, plate `name`, acquisition `name`/`maximumfieldcount`.

**Sources.** S003 capture (version pin in F01), locators: lines 515-739 (section 2.7 plate metadata).

**Implications.** Plate navigation UI (row/column grid, well chooser, field-of-view list) can be built entirely from these fields; the sparse example confirms empty grid cells are normal. The plan's generic image-listing slice needs a plate-aware presentation mode to satisfy the brief's find-images requirement for HCS filesets (with F03 hierarchy and F12 well listing). Name uniqueness plus case-sensitivity caution suggests displaying names verbatim and never case-folding paths.

**Uncertainty.** The capture does not define behavior for wells whose path does not exist on disk, nor how to order multiple fields of view for display; acquisition filtering semantics (viewing one acquisition only) are implied by well-level `acquisition` keys but no UI obligation is stated.

## well metadata: enumerating fields of view

**Finding.** The `well` key sits in the attributes of the well group (S003 lines 740-743). The well dictionary MUST contain `images`, a list of JSON objects specifying all fields of view for the well; each image object MUST contain `path` (string, alphanumeric only, case-sensitive, MUST NOT duplicate any other path in the list); if multiple acquisitions were performed in the plate, each image object MUST also contain `acquisition`, an integer that MUST match one of the acquisition ids defined in the plate metadata (lines 744-750). The well dictionary SHOULD contain `version` (string) (lines 751-752). Examples: a well with four fields across two acquisitions (lines 753-784) and a well with two fields in a four-acquisition plate (lines 785-808).

**Governing conditions.** MUST: `images` list; per-image unique alphanumeric case-sensitive `path`; `acquisition` key when the plate has multiple acquisitions, matching a plate acquisition id. SHOULD: `version`.

**Sources.** S003 capture (version pin in F01), locators: lines 740-808 (section 2.8 well metadata).

**Implications.** Field-of-view selection is metadata-driven: enumerate `well.images`, never directory-scan. Acquisition ids link wells back to plate acquisitions (F11), enabling acquisition-aware filtering if the product wants it. Missing `acquisition` in a multi-acquisition plate is a detectable non-conformance the viewer can report instead of mislabeling fields.

**Uncertainty.** Behavior when `version` is absent is unspecified (it is only SHOULD); whether field paths may point through intermediate groups is not stated (unlike labels, where intermediates are explicitly allowed); ordering of fields for display is unspecified.

## Transitional metadata policy, JSON strictness, and naming style

**Finding.** Transitional metadata is added with the intention of removing it in the future; implementations may be expected (MUST) or encouraged (SHOULD) to support reading it, while writing is usually optional (MAY); examples include custom additions later formalized (S003 lines 60-64). JSON examples in the document may include comments for clarity, but comments MUST NOT be included in JSON objects (lines 65-66). Multi-word keys should use camelCase, though some parts of the specification predate this convention and are to be updated in due course (lines 809-812).

**Governing conditions.** MUST: no comments in JSON objects (strict JSON parsing is safe and correct; comment-tolerant parsing is unnecessary and could mask malformed input). Reading transitional metadata (`bioformats2raw.layout`, `omero`) is the side writers and readers must expect to need; readers MAY be required (MUST) to read it depending on the metadata.

**Sources.** S003 capture (version pin in F01), locators: lines 56-66 (document conventions), 809-812 (section 3 Specification naming style).

**Implications.** The viewer should use a strict JSON parser for all `zarr.json` files and can surface JSON syntax errors as understandable failures (plan Slice 03/05). Interop with real tools (plan Slice 04) requires reading transitional keys, consistent with the transitional policy. Key naming is inconsistent across spec versions (camelCase vs legacy snake_case like `maximumfieldcount` appearing lowercase in examples), so lookups should follow the specification strings exactly, not a naming-style assumption.

**Uncertainty.** The exact future replacement for transitional metadata is unknown; whether field_count vs maximumfieldcount style discrepancies reflect real spec text or capture artifacts cannot be resolved within the frozen corpus.

## Conformance semantics, edition currency, and version history

**Finding.** The capture is the OME-Zarr 0.5 Final Community Group Report, 8 September 2026; this/latest/editor versions all resolve to https://ngff.openmicroscopy.org/0.5/ (S003 lines 1-18). The current released version is 0.5; migration scripts will be provided between numbered versions; data written with the latest changes (an editor's draft) will not necessarily be supported (lines 24-27). Requirement keywords MUST/MUST NOT/REQUIRED/SHALL/SHALL NOT/SHOULD/SHOULD NOT/RECOMMENDED/MAY/OPTIONAL follow RFC 2119 (lines 56-59, 867-874); all specification text is normative except sections explicitly marked non-normative, examples, and notes (lines 875-878). Version history (lines 821-866): 0.5.2 (2025-01-10) clarified that `dimension_names` in axes MUST be included; 0.5.1 (2025-01-10) re-added the improved omero description; 0.5.0 (2024-11-21) introduced Zarr v3 (RFC-2); 0.4.x added bioformats2raw.layout (2022-09-26) and expanded labels; earlier versions trace to 0.1.0 (2020-04-20). The Implementations section says only See Tools (lines 813-814), and citing identifies this edition as 0.5 with doi:10.5281/zenodo.4282107 (lines 815-820).

**Governing conditions.** Normative-text rule lets the reader classify every statement: prose outside examples/notes carries RFC 2119 force. Version history establishes that 0.4-era filesets predate Zarr v3, so a Zarr v3 reader does not automatically read 0.4 filesets.

**Sources.** S003 capture (version pin in F01), locators: lines 1-27 (status), 56-59 (conventions), 809-820 (naming, implementations, citing), 821-866 (version history), 867-896 (conformance, index, references).

**Implications.** The plan's OME-Zarr 0.5 target is pinned to this edition; the viewer should treat `ome.version` 0.5 as its conformance envelope and decide explicitly (product decision) whether to attempt 0.4 filesets, which would additionally require Zarr v2 support. Editor-draft data may not be supported, so version-gated rejections with messages are legitimate. The SHOULD/MUST/MAY split (used throughout F01-F13) is the basis of the obligation-versus-option classification in the report.

**Uncertainty.** The capture's Implementations section is a pointer (See Tools) with no tool content, so actual reader/writer implementation behavior could not be researched within this assignment's source scope; later errata or versions after 8 September 2026 are outside this capture.
